source.title: Interpretable and Steerable Concept Bottleneck Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Akshay R. Kulkarni; T. Weng; V. Narayanaswamy; Shu-Sen Liu; W. Sakla; Kowshik Thopalli

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether a vision SAE covers specified concept sets and reports substantial gaps, refining the claim that dictionary features are complete. It does not test the original toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper reports other SAE interpretability, steerability, and CB-SAE comparison results, but those do not measure the claim versions except for the concept-coverage findings recorded below.
record.test_reason: Expt. 2 measures how many concepts from five predefined sets a 65,536-neuron vision SAE covers. This is a direct, if indirect-construct, test of the V5 completeness claim in a vision encoder. It reports large gaps that the authors say limit the SAE's coverage.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also emphasise that most SAE neurons have low interpretability and/or steerability (only ~19% high on both). They conclude that SAEs capture simple, low-level concepts but miss many user-specified ones, motivating CB-SAE, which they report improves interpretability by 32.1% and steerability by 14.5%.
record.recipe_differences: This is a vision-SAE concept-coverage study using CLIP-Dissect, not a reproduction of the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Measured concept coverage varies with the concept set's size and diversity.

fits_no_version.finding: Only about 19% (12-20% across three SAEs) of SAE neurons score above the mean on both CLIP-Dissect interpretability and steerability; 30-36% score low on both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Most SAE latents in vision encoders are not individually interpretable and causally effective units.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-k and Batch Top-k SAEs have 52,965 and 56,899 of 65,536 neurons dead, versus 4 for the Matryoshka SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The usable dictionary size and the features it recovers depend strongly on SAE architecture.

record.problems: The coverage measurement relies on CLIP-Dissect concept assignments and predefined concept sets. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the coverage values. The study does not test feature stability or canonicality, or the original superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results meeting the row criteria were left out.

untested.parts: Stability of features across seeds or runs, canonicality, and completeness with respect to the model's own variables rather than human concept lists.
All parts (vision encoder SAE, no LLM neuron-spreading or recovery test).

missing.what: Coverage results for the other SAEs: the text states only the CLIP-ViT-L/Vicuna SAE was evaluated for coverage, and no coverage figure appears for the DINOv2 or UnCLIP SAEs. Nothing further needs adding.

record.verdict_notes: Coverage is measured by whether any neuron's CLIP-Dissect best-match concept equals a set item, which is a proxy dependent on CLIP and on the concept set. No uncertainty is reported. The authors are not original sources. Treat the V5 bearing as concept-list completeness, not canonicality.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, and geometry transitions.
Whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The paper studies SAEs on vision-encoder activations, not feature spreading or SAE recovery in LLM internal activations.
Measures concept-set coverage, but not feature stability across runs or whether SAE features are canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

tranche.reason: Expt. 2 reports incomplete coverage of user-specified concepts, qualifying the completeness component of V5.

source_check.notes: Coverage counts unique concepts selected by neuron-wise CLIP-Dissect argmax assignment, rather than an exhaustive inventory of model variables. Appendix A acknowledges assignment reliability and possible feature splitting as limitations.

statements.problem: The coverage figures and conditions are correct, but challenges overstates this study's result: coverage is incomplete rather than absent or reversed.
